_note: Scored rows under results are the gym's own runs on the held-out slice (copied from scoring/scores_test.json; the ai_noether_exact row is the median of three runs of the final reference code: Singular's minAss returns different generating sets from run to run, which moves the weighted score by about +-0.005, see HARDENING.md). The paper's reported numbers are kept under _paper_reported: they were measured on the paper's twelve public theories (this gym's train slice) with a 7200 s timeout, Macaulay2/Singular and the paper's own success criterion, so they are not on the held-out scale. Multi-axiom recovery_rate (decoupled recovery) is a diagnostic: 0 for every honest method on the held-out slice.

single_missing_axiom.description: One axiom is removed from a complete polynomial theory; recover it from the remaining axioms and the target relation (held-out theories, anonymized and unit-rescaled).

recovery_rate.description: Fraction of instances where one of the first five candidate sets is a valid explanation that also recovers every removed axiom: with the known axioms it implies each removed axiom wherever the declared nonzero quantities are nonzero.

explanation_rate.description: Fraction of instances where one of the first five candidate sets is a valid explanation: added to the known axioms it makes every target derivable (ideal membership), every proposed polynomial is a true law of the complete theory wherever the declared nonzero quantities are nonzero (radical membership in the complete theory saturated by their product), and none is already implied by the known axioms, the targets and the targets divided by nonzero monomial factors.

top1_success_rate.description: Fraction of instances whose first-ranked candidate set already succeeds (recovers the removed axiom for single-axiom instances; is a valid explanation for multi-axiom instances).

unsound_rate.description: Constraint: fraction of instances whose first five candidate sets include a set that derives the targets but is false in the complete theory where the nonzero quantities are nonzero (contradiction, forcing a physical quantity to zero, or a stronger-than-true law), plus every instance whose run failed or whose sets could not be verified.

failed_rate.description: Diagnostic: fraction of instances whose run crashed, timed out or wrote malformed output (already counted as worst in every scored metric).

mean_candidate_sets.description: Diagnostic: average number of candidate sets considered per instance (at most five).

instances.description: Diagnostic: number of instances in this experiment, fixed by the evaluator.
